title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§52 of the 'suite à la Longue Marche', p. 691-692). Π_0 ≅ π_1(M_{0,3}) is free of rank 2, embedded in SL(2,Z) as a level-2-type subgroup, with Π_0^{ab} = Π_0/[Π_0,Π_0] ≅ M ≅ Z^2. On the previous page Grothendieck identifies an index-36 subgroup Π_00 of SL(2,Z) as the inverse image of a subgroup Π'_00 of SL(2,Z/12Z), with quotient ≅ [SL(2,F_2)]' × Syl_2. Here [SL(2,F_2)]' = A_3 ≅ Z/3. Inside Π_0, the group Π_00 has index 3, with Π_0/Π_00 ≅ Z/3.

This page draws the geometric consequence. The subgroup Π_00 corresponds to a cyclic étale cover of degree 3 of M_{0,3} over Q̄ = P^1 − {0,1,∞}. Each of the three cusps is totally ramified (ramification index 3). Riemann–Hurwitz gives 2g − 2 = 3(−2) + 3·2 = 0, so g = 1, which Grothendieck says one 'checks immediately'.

The margin identifies the curve: y^3 = x^a(1−x)^b is an elliptic curve with an automorphism of order 3 fixing a point. Hence j = 0, and over Q̄ it is isomorphic to the Fermat cubic x^3 + y^3 = 1. The first margin note links these covers to M_{1,1}.

Next he replaces [Π_0,Π_0] by [Π_00,Π_00].
- Π_00 is free of rank 1 + 3·(2−1) = 4, so Π_00^{ab} ≅ Z^4 = H_1(E°), where E° is the curve minus 3 points.
- Since Π_0/Π_00 is abelian, [Π_0,Π_0] ⊂ Π_00. So Π_0/[Π_00,Π_00] is an extension of M = Π_0^{ab} ≅ Z^2 by K = [Π_0,Π_0]/[Π_00,Π_00] ⊂ Z^4.
- K is torsion-free of rank 4 − 2 = 2. It is (up to finite index) the part of H_1(E°) on which Z/3 acts without fixed vectors, i.e. H_1(E) of the compact curve as a Z[ω]-module. This is what he calls the rank-2 'elliptic' group.

This is a 'relative metabelian' quotient of the free group, adapted to the Fermat cubic. He proposes to study how M acts on this elliptic part. He also wants to relate it to the Galois action and to the comparison map SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ), i.e. the congruence kernel / non-congruence phenomena. These are the objects controlled by the profinite Teichmüller/Galois action in the Longue Marche.

The problem served is understanding the Galois (and SL(2,Z)-outer) action on finite or nilpotent/metabelian quotients of π_1(P^1 − 3 points) through intermediate covers. Here the first nontrivial one is a genus-1 CM curve.
errors: The conjugation action of Π_0 on K = [Π_0,Π_0]/[Π_00,Π_00] ⊂ Π_00^{ab} factors through Π_0/Π_00 ≅ Z/3, acting as multiplication by a cube root of unity on H_1(E). Taken literally, 'M opère de façon hautement non triviale' is overstated. Nontrivial phenomena lie in the extension class (non-central, non-split) and in the outer actions (Galois, SL(2,Z)^), presumably what he really intends to examine.
Minor: K is rank 2 and torsion-free, but its identification with H_1(E) of the compact curve holds only up to finite index; the cusp classes must be accounted for. This is not addressed on the page.

ideas.what: The degree-3 cyclic cover of P^1−{0,1,∞} totally ramified at the three cusps has genus 1 and is the j=0 elliptic curve, isomorphic to the Fermat cubic.
ideas.modern_name: Fermat curve of degree 3 as an abelian cover of the thrice-punctured line (CM elliptic curve with j=0)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Riemann–Hurwitz, Fermat curves); in the Galois-π_1 context Ihara (1985-86), Anderson, Coleman

ideas.what: Replacing the derived subgroup [Π_0,Π_0] by [Π_00,Π_00] of a finite-index subgroup gives an extension of Π_0^{ab} by the homology of the elliptic curve: a relative metabelian quotient of the free group.
ideas.modern_name: Metabelian quotient of π_1(P^1−3pts) relative to Fermat covers; Ihara's universal power series / Fermat Jacobian approach
ideas.usually_credited_to: Y. Ihara (Annals 1986, 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'); G. Anderson (hyperadelic gamma function, 1989); Coleman; Ihara–Kaneko–Yukinari

ideas.what: Program: compare the resulting action on the elliptic part with the action arising from SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ) (congruence kernel).
ideas.modern_name: Galois/outer action on π_1 quotients vs. congruence subgroup kernel; Ĝ T and modular towers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Matsumoto, Asada (1990s), Boggi (congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Galois action on π_1 of moduli and SL(2,Z)^ but not this specific Fermat-cubic metabelian construction

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to study the extension of Π_0^{ab} by H_1 of the Fermat cubic, via [Π_00,Π_00], and to relate the resulting action to SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ). The metabelian/Fermat-curve approach itself was later developed independently (Ihara's Jacobi-sum/CM description of Galois action on Π/Π''). The specific link he proposes is less explored: the elliptic part of this relative metabelian quotient as a probe of the congruence kernel of SL(2,Z), at level 3 inside level 2.
missed.quote: par la suite il me faudrait examiner cette action, et la mettre en relation avec l'action qu'on trouvait ... l'homo SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck anticipating, around 1981, the Fermat-curve/CM approach to Galois action on metabelian quotients that Ihara made rigorous in 1985-86. The connection to the congruence kernel is suggestive but only sketched.

deep.surprise_reason: The geometric facts are routine (Riemann–Hurwitz, j=0 Fermat cubic). The idea of using metabelian quotients relative to the Fermat cover to study Galois/SL(2,Z)^ actions is a genuine, early unpublished anticipation of Ihara–Anderson–Coleman. It is only a sketch, and the direction is well developed in the later literature.
transcription_corrections: 'levit-structures d'ordre 3' should read 'revêtements d'ordre 3 de M_{0,3} Q̄' (the struck-out text after it mentions M_1...).
Margin 1: 'c'est = revêtements M_{1,1} ...' (left margin, near lines 2-4).
'on trouve une groupe extension' → 'on trouve un groupe extension'.
'que on "elliptiques", et sur M on opère' is likely 'qu'on [dira] "elliptique", et sur [lequel] M opère de façon hautement non triviale'.
Margin 2 reads roughly: 'c'est une courbe elliptique d'invariant j=0 (je pense) (courbe de Fermat d'ordre 3) dans la même lignée' — 'ligne' probably 'lignée', uncertain.
Π_{0,0} on this page is the Π_00 of the previous page.
